newsitem.title: USA: Cash crude prices in U.S. swallow more losses.
newsitem.headline: Cash crude prices in U.S. swallow more losses.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. deflated Tuesday afternoon in conjunction with a technically-inspired NYMEX selling spree.
Cash July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing remained firmer than the corresponding July futures price, based on the 13-15 cents premium held by July Exchange for Physicals (EFPs).
Outright cash July WTI/Cushing was pegged 70 cents weaker than late Monday at $20.40-50 a barrel, working off the July NYMEX value of $20.30 a barrel.
NYMEX crude futures losses were extended in early afternoon trade to session lows at $20.28 a barrel, some 70 cents weaker.
On the domestic grade front, most differentials failed to excite large changes from recent price levels.

Midland/WTI was sold at a 37 cents discount, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James moving at 13 and 14 cents under WTI benchmark. West Texas Sour/Midland held ground at last deals of WTI/Cushing -$1.57 and -$1.55.
WTI/Cushing Postings were also steady at $1.95, working against the July/August roll of -15 to -18 cents.

Crude markets looked to the weekly release of inventory data for possible clues on fundamental balances. Expectations for Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute (API) report showed crude stocks building by an average of 313,000 barrels, reflecting calls for both draws and stock increases.

Distillates were also forecast to build, with averages pegged at 2 million barrels. Gasoline stocks, however, were seen drawing 500,000 barrels, and utilization rates expected steady to a shade lower.
Developments outside the market featured a flurry of news briefs on the renewal process for extending the Iraqi oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

All hurdles seem to be clear for renewal of the accord at the present $2 billion oil sales cap. A draft report by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Monday called for such a renewal, a position now favored by the United States.
Action by the Security Council on extending the deal was seen as early as Wednesday, but could come as late as Friday ahead of the current deal's expiration on June 7.
